Subject: Acme - TCO recap & next steps

Hi Alice / Carlos \u0014

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we discussed, the top pain points you called out, and suggested levers we can apply to bring your monthly spend in line with Acme's target: 

Pain points we heard
- Unpredictable token costs during spikes (especially around product launches).
- Heavy per-session generation for summarization + context enrichment (avg session ~320 tokens).
- Desire for a predictable monthly budget and clear cost/levers for procurement.

Goals (what success looks like)
- Reduce per-session generation cost while preserving response quality.
- Keep 95th pct latency under ~250ms for interactive flows.
- Achieve predictable monthly TCO so finance can sign off on a committed plan.

High-level token economics (ballpark)
- Current baseline: ~10M generated tokens / month (you confirmed this number in the call).
- At current list rates we modeled, that maps to ~ $4,000/mo in generation-only spend.
- Peak events can push token volumes 3-5x for short windows, driving delta spend unless smoothed.

Levers we recommend to materially reduce TCO
1) KV/prefix caching: cache common session prefixes (e.g., user prompts + static context) to avoid re-generating tokens for repeated patterns.
2) Continuous batching + request coalescing: groups short requests on the server side to increase GPU utilization and lower per-token compute cost without impacting tail latency for most users.
3) Quantized model variants (4-bit/INT4): For non-critical responses, these can cut compute cost ~30-40% with minimal quality hit.
4) Model routing: route low-criticality completions to smaller/cheaper model variants, keep the larger model for high-value paths.

Attached: Acme-Redwood-TCO-Calc-20260303.xlsx (simple calc showing sensitivity to batch size, cache hit-rate, and quantization). Also a one-pager on Redwood cost controls.

Next steps
- Can you confirm the 10M tokens/month baseline and avg session length (you mentioned ~320 tokens)?
- Rafael to run a short technical feasibility + integration estimate for KV caching + batching with your session store (Redis?) \u0014 target a technical deep-dive next week.
- Ben (cc) will follow up on procurement path / pricing commitment options once we have run-rate estimates.

Thanks again \u0014 looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Thanks Alice \u0014 quick technical notes and feasibility/effort estimates below.

On Tue, Mar 3, 2026 at 6:05 PM Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com> wrote:
> Can Rafael confirm if KV/prefix caching can be implemented to work with our session store (we use Redis currently)?

Short answer: yes \u0014 this is a common integration pattern. Details: 

- KV/prefix caching: Redwood can use a per-session cache key (you already have session ids in Redis). We can either:
  a) Point Redwood's cache layer at your Redis (via a secure read/write endpoint) so cache hits avoid re-generation entirely, or
  b) Implement a lightweight cache sync where Redwood sends cacheable prefix hashes and you maintain the canonical store.
- Expected impact: with a 40% cache-hit rate on warm prefixes you can see ~25-35% reduction in generated tokens for the summarization flow.

- Continuous batching: Redwood's serving runtime supports continuous batching with configurable latency SLOs. For your 250ms 95th target we can tune batching windows and max batch sizes to avoid impacting the tail. Typical configurations reduce per-token CPU/GPU cost by 20-35% while keeping tail latency within SLA for interactive flows.

- Quantized models / model routing: We can evaluate 4-bit quantized variants for your lower-priority flows to save ~30-45% of compute cost. We recommend A/B testing quality on a representative prompt set.

Integration effort & timeline
- Discovery + plan: 2-3 days (collect API/Redis access patterns / auth).
- Engineering integration (cache endpoint + validation): 2-3 weeks with one engineer full-time.
- Testing + A/B quality evals: 1-2 weeks.

Procurement note: If Acme is open to a committed Dedicated plan (reserved capacity), we can provide predictable unit economics that smooths spikes and offers a discount compared to burst-on-hosted pricing. Ben can share commitment tiers \u0014 I'll coordinate with him after we confirm run-rate.

I uploaded a short one-pager and a sample TCO calc to the thread (redwood_tco_onepager.pdf, Acme-Redwood-TCO-Calc-20260303.xlsx). I've also added a slot for a 60m technical deep-dive on my Calendly: https://calendly.com/redwood/tech-deep-dive-60.

If you want, I can prepare a short SOW draft (high level) to include estimated milestones and acceptance criteria for procurement.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
